title: UAP Payout Handler
description:
A pluggable mechanism for moving money to a party in a RevenueSplit. Handlers are namespaced by reverse-DNS and registered the same way UCP registers payment handlers, so an implementation that already resolves UCP handlers resolves these with the same code.

UAP never carries payment credentials. A handler declares where a payout can go and under what terms; the instrument details live with the handler's own provider.

Registered by this specification: dev.uap.payout.ap2 (AP2 settlement mandate, REQUIRED to implement for the uap.settle profile), dev.uap.payout.ach, com.stripe.connect, com.wise.payout.

id.description: Instance identifier, distinguishing multiple configurations of the same handler.

currencies.description: Currencies this handler instance can pay out in.

minimum_payout_micros.description: Balance below which payout is deferred to the next period. A self-hosted node earning a few dollars a month is the common case, so this value determines whether long-tail supply ever actually gets paid; handlers SHOULD keep it low and exchanges MUST NOT expire an undisbursed balance.

payout_period.description: Settlement cadence. Net terms are the norm for holding-company demand; daily and weekly exist so that self-hosted supply is not financing an exchange's working capital.

parties.description: Which RevenueSplit parties this handler instance can pay. A steward payout and a node payout frequently need different rails.

requires_kyc.description: Whether the handler requires identity verification before disbursing. Directly determines the trust tier a seller can reach (SPEC.md §9.3).
